name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yassamin Ansari for Congress
body:
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the full weight of the executive branch bearing down on me right now. |
---
Hey Peter, it’s Mark Kelly. Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate. I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy. But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something. So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too. I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help. We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the full weight of the executive branch bearing down on me right now. After everything you’ve already done for me, I shouldn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do. Our right to vote has never been more important. We've never truly faced threats like this before, and with the midterms coming up fast we have to do everything possible to combat voter suppression, register voters, and ensure we actually have free and fair elections to vote in.
We have to stop the opponents of voting rights before we lose our fundamental right to vote. RUSH $35 or more right now to help us fight back >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=032626_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
“How we have to even run against these people—I won’t say cancel the election, they should cancel the election, because the fake news will say, ‘He wants the elections canceled. He’s a dictator.’ They always call me a dictator."
That was Donald Trump, Team, speaking to members of his party in the House of Representatives on the 5th anniversary of his supporters storming the Capitol to overturn an election he lost.
How many times has Trump "joked" about something he wanted to do before he did it? Too many to count, including weaponizing the government to attack his opponents, his attack on Venezuela, and his attacks on mail-in ballots.
Now, apparently, he's "joking" -- and not for the first time -- about canceling the upcoming midterm elections. It's a threat we all have to take seriously, regardless of party affiliation, because our country was founded on the idea that our voices matter, not just the voices of the powerful.
Pitch in $35 or whatever you can today to help us protect our elections, defend vote by mail, and increase voter participation nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=032626_2&amount=35]

They’re violent, they’re vicious, you know. They’re vicious people .”
He -- and the MAGA propaganda movement at large -- keep saying, in essence, that anyone who doesn't agree with them is sub-human and anyone who doesn't vote for MAGA candidates has something wrong with them, so why bother having elections at all?
They're setting the stage by rewriting history. They're still trying to manufacture evidence to support their lies that the 2020 election was stolen. They've whitewashed the January 6th attack on the Capitol by saying that the police egged the protestors into violence. They're using the Civil Rights division of the Department of Justice to chase internet conspiracy theories. And they threaten investigations and subpoenas into anyone who tries to stop them.

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

#
“**Building Your Safety Ecosystem: Tools for Physical, Digital, and Emotional Safety”**
---
| |

In this challenging political climate, women leaders have encountered harassment, threats, and violence both online and in person, leading many to be concerned about their safety. The DNC wants to be supportive in efforts to promote safety and well-being. In partnership with **Women’s Democracy Lab** , we will host “**Building Your Safety Ecosystem: Tools for Physical, Digital, and Emotional Safety,** ” a training on building a safety ecosystem. This virtual event is designed to help equip people with the knowledge and tools needed to protect themselves while maintaining a visible public presence.
Participants will learn about creating actionable safety plans and developing practical tools to respond to threats. This training is designed to explore the interconnectedness of digital, physical, and emotional safety and how they shape the overall security and well-being of people organizing within their communities. Topics will include:

* Threat awareness and risk assessment
* Digital safety in online harassment
* Physical safety and in-person harassment

**We hope you will be able to join us!**

null, I want to share a bit about my story – and some fun pics! – but I'll give you a heads-up that this is a bit of a longer one. So if you don't have time to read now, I have to ask:
**[Will you rush $5 to help my team and I ensure that we reach our $500,000 goal before the FEC filing deadline on Tuesday? It's our first big deadline of the year, and with Donald Trump watching this race – and our numbers – like a hawk, it couldn't be more important.](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/16043?t=3&akid=2581%2E49239%2ERfw0li)**
| | [RUSH $5 NOW](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/16043?t=4&akid=2581%2E49239%2ERfw0li)
---
[](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/16044?t=5&akid=2581%2E49239%2ERfw0li)
See that little girl in the photo? That’s me! Way before I had the honor of serving Michiganders in Congress and launching this battleground campaign to be Michigan’s next U.S. senator. I was about 12 or 13 years old there.
But don’t be fooled by school picture day (_and my trendy beaded necklace_). Growing up as the daughter of small-business owners – Mom and Dad had their own landscaping business – I was always around a lot of dirt, grease, grime, and heavy machinery. **I wouldn’t have had it any other way.**
My parents taught me the value of hard work – a value that binds all of us in Michigan together. After all, we’re the state that built America. The state that built the middle class.
In fact, do you know what one of my favorite memories is from growing up? When I got the keys to my first car, a used Oldsmobile Cutlass Supreme. That car represented the newfound freedom of teenage years. **It wasn’t quite the showstopper you usually see at the Woodward Dream Cruises, but it got the job done and it took my all over our beautiful state.**
[](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/16044?t=6&akid=2581%2E49239%2ERfw0li)
**I love Michigan. I love the people here. And I love that I’ve been able to fight for my state in Congress.
**
But as I’ve traveled our state recently, it’s clear that the people I love are afraid. They’re afraid because of the chaos and uncertainty that Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are inflicting upon our nation.
All across our state, I hear concerns about rising costs, unaffordable health care, and the future of Social Security and Medicare.

And you better believe people are outright disturbed by Trump’s attacks on our democracy and personal freedoms. **This fear, uncertainty, and chaos – all of it is**** _unacceptable._**
That’s why I’m running for U.S. Senate. I’m ready to fight for the people I love and help block Trump’s dangerous agenda. But the path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan – **and right now, we're up against our first official FEC deadline of the election year.**
**null, we can't show any weakness here.** Donald Trump and his megadonor allies are waiting to pounce, and they'll throw millions at this race the second they see an opening.
**We can't give them one. It's crucial that we make a strong showing with our first 2026 FEC report, so I have to ask: _[Will you rush $5, $25, or whatever you can to help us reach our $500,000 goal before the deadline hits?](https://act.haleyformi.com/go/16044?t=7&akid=2581%2E49239%2ERfw0li)_**

**A note from Haley Stevens:** null, I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. That’s why I’ve fought so hard for working families my entire life. Now, I’m running for Michigan’s open Senate seat to continue fighting for the people and communities I love. The path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan, which means this race is shaping up to be the most competitive and expensive in the entire country. The GOP is already coming after me as a top target for defeat, so I’m counting on your grassroots support to fight back and win. name: Virginians For Fair Elections
subject: 🚨 Early vote update: this is a warning sign
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260326-396&t=2&akid=396%2E12592%2ENLjDAI)
[](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260326_2.XGB6Z9&amount=3&refcode=20260326-396&t=3&akid=396%2E12592%2ENLjDAI)
In some parts of Virginia, turnout is higher in Republican-led areas right now. That tells us MAGA Republicans are showing up early and falling in line behind Donald Trump’s push to tilt the playing field before the midterms.
[**Can you help us fight back and turn the tide on this vote? We need to overcome Republicans’ numbers and their misinformation that is flooding the Commonwealth.**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260326_2.XGB6Z9&amount=3&refcode=20260326-396&t=4&akid=396%2E12592%2ENLjDAI)
That’s the bad news.
Here’s the good news: **this election is far from decided.**
Millions of ballots are still left to be cast. Virginia voters still have the power to level the playing field and make sure the 2026 elections are decided by people, not politicians.
But only if we match their energy.
Early voting is already underway. Election Day is April 21. And this race is shaping up to come down to enthusiasm and turnout in these final weeks.
Right now this is the state of the election:
* Turnout is ahead in Republican-held areas
* Some polls show the YES vote trailing, while others show it within reach
* This will come down to who shows up and who gets reached in time

Meanwhile, MAGA-funded misinformation is flooding mailboxes and feeds across the Commonwealth, trying to confuse voters and slow our momentum.
_That’s why we’re going all in._
But here’s the reality: **reaching the voters who will decide this election takes resources, and we’re up against big money trying to block this amendment.**
We cannot afford to fall behind right now. If we’re going to win, we need to expand our outreach, stay on the air, and keep building momentum through Election Day.
[**Will you rush a donation of $3 or whatever you can to help power this final push?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260326_2.XGB6Z9&amount=3&refcode=20260326-396&t=5&akid=396%2E12592%2ENLjDAI)
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260326_2.XGB6Z9&amount=3&refcode=20260326-396&t=24&akid=396%2E12592%2ENLjDAI)**
This is a close election. We always knew it would be. But this moment is a flashing red warning sign, and also an opportunity.
If we act now, if we meet this moment with everything we have, we can still win this and protect fair elections for years to come. Let’s not look back and wonder what more we could have done. **We don’t want to wake up with regrets on April 22.**
Let’s do all we can right now to fight back and win.
Thank you for being with us,
Virginians for Fair Elections

clean_body: A lot has changed since 1985 — but EMILYs List is still here to meet the moment. | = NEW: A 3X match for the month of March. Every online gift will be tripled through March 31 — until we reach $500,000 and unlock $1.5M for EMILYs List women. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = = = Dear Peter, So much has changed since EMILYs List’s founding in 1985 — including so much that I could never have expected back then. I founded EMILYs List in a time before social media, before misinformation could spread instantly on the internet, and long before Donald Trump became a central figure in our politics. But another thing I didn’t expect to see today? A 3X digital match campaign of this scale — the largest in our organization’s history. From now until the end of March, EMILYs List leaders and longtime supporters will triple-match all grassroots contributions up to $500,000 — unlocking $1.5 million to support women running in tough races in 2026. This match is a rare opportunity to make grassroots support go further when it matters most. = = Over the next week, you’ll also hear directly from members of our board about why this match matters and why they’re invested in meeting this moment. I’m excited for you to hear from them — and grateful they’re lending their voices as we work to unlock the full $1.5 million. I never thought that I’d be living through a political moment like this one — but I’m proud that EMILYs List is here to help fund, train, and elect the women ready to fight back and stand up for our rights. We’re working with battle-tested candidates running for office up and down the ballot — from statehouses to the U.S. House — to take back power in 2026. We’ll be facing a well-funded opposition in tight states and districts where every vote matters. Now, it is no coincidence that the conservative Supreme Court is predicted to rule in favor of allowing states to ban mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day, **a decision that could cancel out the vote of millions of Americans.**

With the midterm elections just months away, the stakes couldn’t be higher.

body:
Do you have a moment?

| | |
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7218?t=1&akid=8543%2E400544%2EZNix2j)
Friend,

Before Women's History Month comes to an end, I want to take a moment to share how proud I am to come from generations of resilient and fierce Pueblo women.

It's moments like these where I find myself thinking more about my great-grandmother, mother, and many before them who have taught me to Be Fierce — to protect our communities and never back down.
And that’s exactly what I’ve done. I’ve stood up to corporate polluters. I rebuilt the Department of the Interior after Trump slashed staff, cut budgets, and rolled back protections. I defended our public lands and our people when they were under attack.
**
And I won’t stop now.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7218?t=2&akid=8543%2E400544%2EZNix2j)
---
Friend, Trump and his allies are doing everything to tear us down. Gutting healthcare. Raising costs. Ignoring the affordability crisis. Empowering ICE to terrorize families and sow fear in our neighborhoods. Dismantling our voting rights. Attacking reproductive freedom and dividing us to hold on to power. **_Destroying our democracy._**
I’m fighting back.

I was a single mom. I relied on Medicaid, WIC, and SNAP. I worked multiple jobs and started a small salsa business to get by. I know how to keep fighting even when it feels like it isn’t getting any easier — and Trump definitely isn’t making it any easier.

That’s why I’m prepared to lead.
I understand affordability because I’ve lived it. I know how critical strong public schools, accessible healthcare, and safe communities are because my family relied on them.

And I’ve led at the highest levels of government — in Congress and as U.S. Secretary of the Interior — where I took on tough fights and delivered real results.

**_Experience matters. Leadership matters. And I’m ready to be the governor for all New Mexicans._**
But at a time when women are being sidelined by the Trump administration, we must work even harder to protect, uplift, and stand together. **I will always be a champion for women's rights and fight for our communities, friend, but I can't do it without you.

[In honor of Women's History Month, would you consider making a contribution of $5 to my campaign for governor before our end-of-quarter deadline? Together, we will build a future that honors women and where everyone can thrive.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7224?t=3&akid=8543%2E400544%2EZNix2j)**

body:
Billionaires have rigged this system in their favor for too long. It’s time to even the score for working families.Header
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260326-6055-footer&t=1&akid=6055%2E420207%2Exu9QjD)
Peter,
I’ve spent years taking on our broken tax system. And I need you to know: this week felt different.
**Washington State just passed the Millionaires Tax — a 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, a historic first for my home state.**
This is a _huge_ win for working families. And it’s only the beginning. The new Millionaires Tax will put over $4 billion a year to work. Funding free school meals, childcare, and tax credits.
This is the fight I’ve built my career on — and I'm taking this energy right back to Congress.
Alongside Senator Elizabeth Warren, I just reintroduced the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act. This legislation would:
* Set a 2% annual tax on wealth over $50 million
* Apply a 3% tax on wealth over $1 billion
* Raise at least $3 trillion over 10 years to invest in universal health care, childcare, education, housing, and clean energy

A fairer economy starts here — one that works for everyone, not just the wealthy few at the top.
Here’s the reality of what we’re up against: the richest 1% of Americans own more than 30% of the country’s wealth, but only pay 3.2% of that wealth in taxes. Working families pay **twice** as much. And while we’re fighting to fix that, Trump and his Republican allies in Congress are trying to hand billionaires _another_ massive tax cut.
I refuse to accept that, and I know you won’t either.
**Here in Washington State, we’re showing the nation what it looks like to put working people first. Now it’s time to take that fight to every corner of this country, and make sure the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share.**
[**The mega-rich have rigged this system to protect their interests for decades. Will you pitch in $3 today to help keep me in the fight and finally even the score for working people?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260326-2.9UoyBm&refcode=em20260326-6055&amount=3&t=2&akid=6055%2E420207%2Exu9QjD)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

subject: Winning in our new CA congressional maps:

Hi friends , it’s been a few months since California voters overwhelmingly passed Prop 50 and established updated congressional districts to counter Trump’s midterm power grab.
I want to take a second to talk about what winning in these new maps looks like, and what you can do to help.
First, let’s talk CA-51:
My district was actually made a bit more competitive in the new maps, by about 4-5 points.
It was stretched to the east, absorbing areas previously in the 48th District (represented currently by Republican Darrell Issa). I’m so excited to welcome voters in areas like Julian and Lakeside and I look forward to being out on the campaign trail getting to know new folks.
And it’s not just my race I’m worried about — over the next seven months or so, I’m going to be reaching out to this team about important races to track and ways to get involved all over the country.
But today, I’m asking my strongest supporters to chip in to my own re-election campaign ahead of our March 31st FEC filing deadline. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
After these filing deadlines, reports are published for anyone and everyone to see — the press, the pundits, Republican candidates and operatives — and what’s inside them can make a big difference in a campaign’s future.
A strong report can discourage Republican challengers and outside special interest spending. A weak one can do the opposite!
Representing CA-51 in Congress is a huge honor — and one I don’t take for granted for a single second. I’ll be out on the campaign trail this year to listen to constituents about their concerns and priorities, and share how I plan to support them if I’m elected to serve a fourth term.
If you can, please consider contributing to my re-election campaign so I can keep up this work and make sure I’m ready to deliver a strong victory in November. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]

**Peter, I know we’ve all got a lot on our minds these days. **
I’m a mom of 3 - I get it.

| | Health care premiums are out of control. Trump's war in Iran is threatening to spiral and has already caused gas prices to skyrocket. The administration continues to ignore federal courts in its attempt to institute tariffs on the American people. So what's the top priority of Senate Republicans this week? **Voter suppression.** At Trump's direction, Senate Republicans opened debate last week on the deceptively titled "SAVE America Act." The SAVE Act is nothing short of a voter suppression bill that Trump is trying to cram through the Senate just before the midterms, because he knows his agenda of pardoning pedophiles and jacking up health care costs isn't cutting it for the American people. If passed into law, this bill would require a passport to register to vote. Fifty percent of Americans don't have a valid passport. This provision would be particularly devastating for married women, many of whom don't have a passport with their new last name if they changed it after marriage. It would require in-person voter registration at county elections offices, which would be a huge blow to seniors and rural voters. And lastly, it takes aim at vote-by-mail, which Oregonians have been using for over 30 years. It would unravel our elections as we know it. This is a calculated attempt to suppress the vote ahead of the midterms in November. [**Will you join in opposing the SAVE Act? clean_body: | | | | Health care premiums are out of control. Trump's war in Iran is threatening to spiral and has already caused gas prices to skyrocket. The administration continues to ignore federal courts in its attempt to institute tariffs on the American people. So what's the top priority of Senate Republicans this week? Voter suppression. At Trump's direction, Senate Republicans opened debate last week on the deceptively titled "SAVE America Act." The SAVE Act is nothing short of a voter suppression bill that Trump is trying to cram through the Senate just before the midterms, because he knows his agenda of pardoning pedophiles and jacking up health care costs isn't cutting it for the American people. If passed into law, this bill would require a passport to register to vote. Fifty percent of Americans don't have a valid passport. This provision would be particularly devastating for married women, many of whom don't have a passport with their new last name if they changed it after marriage. It would require in-person voter registration at county elections offices, which would be a huge blow to seniors and rural voters. And lastly, it takes aim at vote-by-mail, which Oregonians have been using for over 30 years. It would unravel our elections as we know it. This is a calculated attempt to suppress the vote ahead of the midterms in November. body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105299?t=6&akid=23384%2E878179%2EMFG9T3) Today’s my birthday, and I couldn’t be more grateful for the outpouring of birthday wishes I am receiving from so many of you. You know that your support means so much to me!

[I’ll share my birthday wish with you: What I want most for my birthday is your help to TAKE BACK THE HOUSE for our Democrats and STOP Donald Trump’s assault on our freedoms, on our health care and on the livelihoods of America’s working families. Will you split $10 between my leadership PAC, PAC to the Future, and the Voter Protection Project, so we can RUSH resources to Democrats on the frontline, FLIP the House and finally put a check on Trump’s incompetence and abuses of power?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105586?t=7&akid=23384%2E878179%2EMFG9T3)

Our nation is in the midst of a crisis after Trump and Republicans in Congress have practically abolished the constitutional role of Congress this term.

**FIRST:** Mike Johnson **GUTTED** Medicaid to give TRILLIONS in tax breaks to his ultra-wealthy donors in their Big Ugly Bill.

**THEN:** Republicans’ approval ratings plummeted along with their chances to keep their **RAZOR-THIN MAJORITY** in the House.

**NOW:** Republicans in Texas, North Carolina and Missouri **RIGGED** 7 House seats to insulate Trump from accountability from voters and hand him another dangerous Majority.

**And last night, Donald Trump headlined House Republicans’ biggest fundraiser of the year to CRUSH our chance at a historic Blue Wave.**

[I am not exaggerating when I say this could be our last chance to rescue our Democracy. So please: I need your help to generate a RECORD-BREAKING response – 10,000 gifts before midnight – to help our Democrats reclaim the House, ELECT Leader Hakeem Jeffries Speaker and hold Donald Trump and his corrupt MAGA accomplices accountable. Will you help me celebrate by splitting $10 or whatever you can between PAC to the Future and the Voter Protection Project before my birthday ends? It would truly mean the most to see your name on my list of donors!](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105586?t=8&akid=23384%2E878179%2EMFG9T3) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between PAC to the Future and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105587?t=9&akid=23384%2E878179%2EMFG9T3)

| | Friends,
It's go time, and I'm ready to win in November if you are.
Tomorrow delegates and alternates will decide who will carry our party's banner for Attorney General into one of the most important midterm elections in the country.
The question isn't complicated: Who can win in November?
Throughout this campaign, I've traveled across Michigan, met with delegates, answered your questions, and earned your trust.
I haven't just talked, I've shown up. I didn't shy away from debates because you deserve the chance to look under the hood. Many of you even have my cell phone number. That's intentional. I believe you deserve direct answers, not scripted ones.
I've also kept this campaign positive and focused on the issues that matter. This race is too important to get sidetracked by last-minute lies and attacks from my opponent.
Winning will take more than a message. It takes experience, discipline, and a candidate who can compete statewide and strengthen the entire Republican ticket.
We are up against a well-funded Democratic machine that will be nominating a progressive prosecutor. I am the only candidate who can counter that agenda and attract independent and moderate Democratic voters. When you nominate me, it will also unlock the broad financial support needed to compete and win in November.
I bring the experience and the merit-based endorsements that matter.
You and I have built a grassroots army.
We have support from local law enforcement leaders across Michigan.
This is the campaign we have built together to win in November.
On Saturday, you're not just voting for a nominee, you're deciding whether we're serious about winning this race.
I'm asking for your vote at the convention. Let's unite to take back the Attorney General's office.
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General
P.S. Join us Friday night at our convention reception. I'm looking forward to thanking the incredible people we've met along this journey to restore Michigan. Stop by and grab an "Elect Doug Lloyd" shirt while supplies last.

## Trump Orders DHS to Pay TSA Agents
President Trump said Thursday he would [sign an emergency order](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHO4yAQBeDT4A4LBtYkBcU27rLtltbEDDErbCyYxPLtV84V_m6kkd7T9_4-pgemnLbXH1zJcyzTRkfLxEx14vpe91ID1cYNdzzfbW8VmSZQMEhlJLgpYMrnZLvgIxGQ6chr5-ygBoChW7yDuwVyN-PsDWIApbWJEAfzy8zontQlf6UpA04rrcD0Cm_uHmzQWoU5BhRWUUhcav-vpI0XivksH6r9XNYu-4V5b8L8FjAKGI_j6OdnuxTXX8B4nQLGL0Z-NZIbyh1PiU2Gpcm2vDmUY5Oh4qvJsgkYu-rDfqScUxucsOq1YsrfRv7RTB8P_wMAAP__TdB9zg) directing the Homeland Security secretary to immediately start paying TSA agents again, stepping in as Congress remained deadlocked over funding for the Department of Homeland Security. Senate Majority Leader John Thune delivered what he called a ["last and final" offer](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdKDFdgwULq6hy7VXIsMuwZHBlr0E5e1P_K_wd580o5nR_HtOT-eDP15_3U6W1zgddJVAzJQnzueeYkbKhYtL7nuWVLJjmiRIU4OqZTeh8-E76QrtSiRJVWTbrtMGjJSm2uxjprmlntSAyqxm6XuA7qH1irqf3ewqb-80ULJroQWpGnB9N6DGtgVcVnRCA6HnmJt39AdvtIZv_FBulrhXwW7MqQj1R8hRyPG6ribF4Nkv8TYIOQb_ofpM6JiKkOPdJuQI6uablni8MpVbe8ftqHk7D6pxKzWSCzVAr40ahipbTJcPwRfTCQ2v3fnws4F_ddzHyv8BAAD__35vgU0) to Democrats on Thursday, and senators prepared to stay through the night to reach a deal before a two-week recess. The GOP proposal would fund most of DHS but leave out money for ICE's enforcement and removal operations, the central sticking point. More than 480 TSA officers have quit since the shutdown began, callout rates have topped 40% at some airports, and wait times have [exceeded four hours](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO6yAQheGnwR0RDFzjFBS3cZdtt7RYZohZYWPBJNm8_Sp5ha2P9Evf-bwsl5BL3q8fYSPPqS47PXohZmoLt9t21IbUOvdwhOetH70FpgUUjFIZCW7BkMtzsQP6RARkBvLaOTuqEWAcVj-NeLZABF-IzpkYdXIpGXRnG6O205D9q6YMOK20AnNSYXJntKi1wpgwCKsIM9d2-q5555VSedY7tVOs21D8ynx0Yf4LmAXMvNKaS3ltAua1bvQCCZg77YFJwPxvUjBpI6_1kG-h5B4k_VC8cb6TDJFz3QXMQ_N4PHIpuY9OWHXdQn6HB_7TU3cPvwEAAP__H5l-jQ). Assaults on TSA officers have surged more than 500% during the standoff.
## US Extends Pause on Hitting Iran Energy Sites
President Trump on Thursday extended a pause on strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure until April 6, a 10-day delay to allow negotiations. [Read the announcement here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MHK4yAUBeCnibsWvRpNFy4Ghuw6q4FZhhu9aRxMDHrb0rf_yf8K__Yc-OCcf_fpjimn_fEHN_K8lGmnd8vETHXi-tyOUiPVxg0P_Dzb0SoyTSDBXqS-gJsipvyZjIh-IQLSgrxyzlhpAaxYfa_6MNtgl17aMBuJBggphnle7GzdIJI_NanBKakk6KvEwd2iiUrJGJaInZEUE5d6_V_Szist-VNeVK-hbCL7lflonf7VwdjByPXJayshYT77MzSyEubfZccc_56TOhiP0rh1MCpl4ebg1vdGD3pwyonq4_FOOadmXWfkY8P0TQn-0T8vD18BAAD__8xqeTs). Trump said talks with Tehran are "going very well" even as Iran continues to deny any direct negotiations are taking place. The Strait of Hormuz [remains effectively shut](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb_GbEa2IZgMHrqwpWtH9IKfw2sNRvYjKP36ivxC13ulq3vO1228AUVaH5-woOOQxhWPEpEZ88h5X7aUPebCBTZ47WUrGRhHo0wnVSONHT1QfI1t5V1ANNhU6LS1bac6Y7pqdqHFJuir1_6i7n3XXHurdLBWK7xfeoSK3LmmGmO10so0tYLeXn3rtVZ-Ch5Eq9ATp1x_J1p5xhBf6Ym5ntJSRTczb0U0H8IMwgzHcdTTvZwUZy_MEOmJct88MBZhBsqwygOyfNNJKhkwSsb5zD2uhEVOCAUDZZQM8afIwhmIZQpyTnnZf4UZquz8dlCMVDorWvVYgOL7Ef9L49OZvwAAAP__vTmKvQ), and Iran continued attacking Persian Gulf states and Israel on Thursday. Israel said it killed the Iranian naval commander responsible for the Hormuz blockade in a targeted airstrike. Oil prices rose more than 5% on Thursday, with Brent crude closing above $108 a barrel, while the [S&P 500 fell 1.74%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb8GOww8GHUKim3sZtstzVMeIxsUA8wQ_37j_MJ2J7nJubn35zE90Ae_P79xI1NcnHaqOVAplKaSXtsRk6WUS8YDz1c-csJCEwjouFAc-smiD-ekG2scEZBqyMi-153oALpmNUBwm9FqWu6D0_NtcCiVVPdumAenBmi8uWxCQS-FFKBagUN_t9pKKeziLDItyPoSU_sb_V5WcuGMb0rtErcmmLWUIzP1xWBkMNZa22WflytkMF5qBqNQF1_02cR9wp1XTDz6wGmn9Dz5ga9M7Vq20CRjj-pD8LnrmRbPDX34tJV_XfQ28BcAAP__mKp6jQ), its sharpest single-day drop in over two months. Gas prices nationally have climbed to an average of $3.98 a gallon, up roughly 33% in a month.
## Olympics Bar Biological Males from Women's Events
The International Olympic Committee on Thursday [banned biological males](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM6agcWQmINjE7G26odVKq2whWNDzLP9-i_2FF_UJus69df98TV8YYkjbbzzI8ZqnRFeNxExl4vI5zlw8lcoVT7w_9awFmSZQMEhlJNjJY4j31HferURApiOnre0HNQAM3e6exsLTeo3wnAeNy7Boa14GYX73ajamC67ZlAGrlVZgHgpf9u17r7Xyy-pR9Ip84Fwef3NIvNMa7_xN5bHko4tuZz6rML8EjALG67oen4qcPd7tQcBYOZe73TMXrgLGHO_jDEvDFi1gVKZxo5AXOWOqkgumulHyVCTyHompypm2kFJIm4y5SkwbRapyw4Oa7PU28O5fSikrYOyK8-cVYgx1sKJX24Eh_u_MPxr628G_AAAA__-POZGC) from competing in women's events at the Olympics, starting with the 2028 Los Angeles Games. This reverses a policy first adopted in 2004 that allowed transgender women to compete after undergoing sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy. IOC President Kirsty Coventry, a two-time Olympic swimming gold medalist, announced the change Thursday. Women will now be required to undergo a one-time screening for the SRY gene, a genetic marker found on the male Y chromosome. Senate Majority Leader John Thune delivered what he called a to Democrats on Thursday, and senators prepared to stay through the night to reach a deal before a two-week recess. The GOP proposal would fund most of DHS but leave out money for ICE's enforcement and removal operations, the central sticking point. More than 480 TSA officers have quit since the shutdown began, callout rates have topped 40% at some airports, and wait times have . Assaults on TSA officers have surged more than 500% during the standoff. US Extends Pause on Hitting Iran Energy Sites President Trump on Thursday extended a pause on strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure until April 6, a 10-day delay to allow negotiations. . Trump said talks with Tehran are "going very well" even as Iran continues to deny any direct negotiations are taking place. The Strait of Hormuz , and Iran continued attacking Persian Gulf states and Israel on Thursday. Israel said it killed the Iranian naval commander responsible for the Hormuz blockade in a targeted airstrike. Oil prices rose more than 5% on Thursday, with Brent crude closing above $108 a barrel, while the , its sharpest single-day drop in over two months. Gas prices nationally have climbed to an average of $3.98 a gallon, up roughly 33% in a month. Olympics Bar Biological Males from Women's Events The International Olympic Committee on Thursday from competing in women's events at the Olympics, starting with the 2028 Los Angeles Games. This reverses a policy first adopted in 2004 that allowed transgender women to compete after undergoing sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy. IOC President Kirsty Coventry, a two-time Olympic swimming gold medalist, announced the change Thursday. ## Arrest Made in 1990 Cold Case
The Harris County District Attorney's Office has charged Floyd William Parrott, 64, with the 1990 murders of Cheryl Henry, 22, and Andy Atkinson, 21. He [was arrested](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp8Gd0T8OBAKim3c3W23tCYwDuhiiGByE7_9yvsKWx7N6OjT-fO1fkEuuT5-w46ePltbK75HQSLs657HyPWxlfxIBERYI1TaYKxKKMOF5squEXI51nmK_i6ikxN6ae1shFPOTMlHDRH0HN1st9tVmXBzMtgthPvV6lmoKftTJrSyUgqp9cUEKQBMkIjmCnBjs8CYqfULJST8wNjK0X6wX0Lbp-IT0XMw_YuphakF7kHq88LU8myDmFrK-Tx4gYp8f_V4AvSOg_gOEbl0TvD3iam9BrXKv3M5o_CQsB-FJ6z94FDjwYG-cx2tcnhRaj1TxsEHHEwt8matE84wtUzdx-f7lAxj2SweO-Tyby79X-Qfr_4GAAD__4xPkzM) on Wednesday in Lincoln, Nebraska, and is being extradited to Houston. Henry and Atkinson were last seen Aug. 22, 1990, after leaving a nightclub in west Houston, and their bodies [were discovered](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu5SAQRb8GdzzhwWC7oNjGXbbd0hrD8IyCTQSTOPn7ld8vpByNdO6959_b-oYpp_P5Fw9y_B3LetLVMjFTXY_UWjqfMafnzshMZ8CTI7YVFFiptIRxDZjyzzp0wW0qzH1Hrh_HwaoZZtvtzswQUG_bZEeljZmnYCOaIY4Gg54VdMndMKVh7HvVa_2wvleI1vdE1iBOYlAUEpf64J2YvrHF_FO-qD58ObrsduaPJvQfAYuA5bqux_tePu-ngAUrJ59JwHLvErD4mo77zDehyYwnyfeUbwdN-pKD9NhIYq3UWO7ls3E55StWwAKTkTHAZjZj5TZ5kkPwXk6DITkZj9FPqGbUXXXh47qxzY5iUM8DU3715d9Z_nLwPwAA___dN5FV) the next day in an area known as Lovers Lane. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
Newsletter from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-kqs1grv7ud-12933068?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
# NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,

**Sine Die marks the close of the 2026 Legislative Session,** and I am grateful for the opportunity to serve our district and state these past 60 days. I want to thank my colleagues, staff, and all those who contributed to making this session a success. Together, we worked to advance priorities that strengthen our communities and move Florida forward.
While the regular session has concluded, **we will be returning to Tallahassee for a special session at the end of April** to continue work on key issues, including the state budget and other top priorities.
As always, please do not hesitate to [**contact my office**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=ee15389cb3&e=d1c1b9864f) if there is something we can do for you. My team and I would be more than happy to help you in any way we can.
---
| |
# Resolution Filed and Published
---
|
---
| | **I am proud to have sponsored**[**House Ceremonial Resolution 8103**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=13c66b478f&e=d1c1b9864f)**to designate May 10, 2026, as First Responders Mental Health Awareness Day in Florida.**
Our law enforcement officers, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, and dispatchers face unimaginable stress and trauma in the line of duty. While they work tirelessly to protect our communities, we must also ensure they have the support, resources, and encouragement they need to care for their own mental health.
This resolution is about breaking the stigma, promoting access to critical services, and sending a clear message: taking care of your mental health is a sign of strength.
**To all of our first responders — thank you for your sacrifice, your courage, and your unwavering commitment to keeping Florida safe.** We stand with you.
---
| |
# Events in the Capitol and District
---
|
---
| | **I enjoyed attending our final Legislative Prayer Breakfast of the session.** We were also honored to have a special guest, 2025 The Voice winner Adam David, who delivered a powerful performance of “Hard Fought Hallelujah.”
What a great way to begin our wrap up of another legislative session.
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Congratulations to VOCAL – Voices of Change Animal League on a fantastic 10th Annual Furball.** It was a great night in support of an incredible nonprofit that continues to make a meaningful difference for animals in our community.
**Raising $809,883 toward their nonprofit and capital campaign** for expansion is an incredible achievement and will help VOCAL continue expanding their reach and impact.
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Congratulations to Empath Health on the ribbon cutting of the Nancy Renyhart Dementia Education Center.** The strong turnout reflects how meaningful this new resource will be for families across our region.
This project was made possible in part through state funding secured by our office alongside Senator McClain, helping transform the facility into a space dedicated to dementia education and support services for caregivers and loved ones.
To learn more about dementia resources and educational opportunities, visit: [**https://hospiceofmarion.org/dementia/**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=7809a5dfa1&e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| |
# Recent Meetings in Tallahassee:
---
|
---
| | **It was a privilege to meet with representatives from Pregnancy and Family Resource Alliance and Personhood Florida** to discuss the important work they are doing to support women, children, and families across our state.
From providing critical resources and counseling to advocating for policies that strengthen protections for the unborn, these organizations are on the front lines serving some of the most vulnerable in our communities. Their commitment to life, compassion, and family-centered support makes a meaningful difference every day.
Thank you for taking the time to share your insights and for your continued dedication to Florida’s families. I look forward to continuing the conversation on how we can work together to ensure both mothers and babies have the support they need to thrive.
---
|
---
|
---
| | **I had a productive meeting with Second Harvest Food Bank of Central Florida** to discuss their expansion plans in Marion County and the growing need for food assistance in our community.
Second Harvest plays a critical role in partnering with local nonprofits and community organizations to fight food insecurity, and their plans to expand in Marion County will help reach even more neighbors in need. I appreciate their commitment to serving our region and look forward to supporting efforts that strengthen resources for families across our community.
---
|
---
|
---
| | **It was a pleasure meeting Mary Connolly, a proud Ocala constituent who is making a difference both academically and professionally.**
Mary is currently a student at the University of Central Florida and is serving as a Legislative Intern for Representative Kaylee Tuck. It’s always encouraging to see young leaders from our community stepping up to serve and gaining firsthand experience in the legislative process.
Ocala continues to produce outstanding students who are committed to public service, and Mary is a great example of that bright future. Wishing her continued success as she works toward her goals!
---
|
---
|
---
| | **It was great to see my friend Courtney Ballestero from the Florida Early Childhood Advocacy Fellowship to discuss the importance of investing in early childhood education and care across our state.**
Strong early learning opportunities lay the foundation for lifelong success, and it’s encouraging to see passionate advocates working to strengthen policies that support Florida’s children, families, and educators. Thank you, Courtney, for your dedication to ensuring every child has the opportunity to thrive from the very start. It was great to see my friend Courtney Ballestero from the Florida Early Childhood Advocacy Fellowship to discuss the importance of investing in early childhood education and care across our state.
Strong early learning opportunities lay the foundation for lifelong success, and it’s encouraging to see passionate advocates working to strengthen policies that support Florida’s children, families, and educators. Thank you, Courtney, for your dedication to ensuring every child has the opportunity to thrive from the very start.
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Enjoyed a quick meet and greet with Americans for Prosperity.**
Appreciate the opportunity to connect, exchange ideas, and continue the conversation about policies that support freedom, opportunity, and a strong future for Florida. Looking forward to staying in touch!
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Enjoyed sitting down with the American Conservation Coalition to discuss the future of conservation and responsible environmental stewardship.** We had a thoughtful conversation about protecting Florida’s natural resources while promoting economic growth and innovation.
From expanding clean energy solutions to preserving our waterways and public lands, it’s encouraging to see young leaders engaged and bringing forward-thinking ideas to the table. I appreciate their passion for practical, market-driven approaches that keep Florida beautiful for generations to come.
---
|
---
| |
# Other Key Remarks:
---
|
---
| | **Congrats to our Speaker Danny Perez** on the unveiling of his portrait today, It will hang in this chamber for the next 100 years.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Rep. Yvette Benarroch, Rep. Meg Weinberger, Rep. Sam Greco, Rep. Vanessa Oliver, Rep. Bill Conerly, Rep. Nan Cobb, Rep. Nathan Boyles, Rep. Brian Hodgers
---
| | Meet my colleagues I've shared the 14th floor the past 2 years with at the Capitol. We're looking forward to wrapping up this session and we will all be getting new office assignments come November.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | **It was great to have Allison Leibfried serving as a Page this week, during this year’s Legislative Session!**
The House Page Program gives students a unique opportunity to experience the legislative process up close while assisting with the day-to-day operations of the Capitol. Allison did a fantastic job representing our community and stepping up to serve during session.
Thank you, Allison, for your hard work and for taking part in this great program!
---
|
---
| | Thank you for your continued support of my leadership in the Florida House! I look forward to sharing with you again soon.
Best regards,
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **Ryan Chamberlin****State Representative****District 24**

name: Christina Hines
subject: Saturday Action: Turn Protest into Progress
body:
Hi team CH4C,

We have a big opportunity this weekend to turn energy into action - and I’d
love for you to be part of it.

For those attending the Macomb County Hall Road location of the No Kings
protest, we’ll be meeting at the vacant Citizen’s bank at Hall Rd &
Schoenherr at 10:30 AM. The address is *13620 Northbay Dr, Sterling
Heights, MI 48313*.

George Higgins will be there with everything you need - CH4C t-shirts,
literature, and QR codes for both volunteering and donations:
[image: Copy of Hines Brand Templates (1080 x 1080 px) (2).jpg]

Here’s the goal: talk to as many people as you can. Share a quick version
of why you’re involved and invite them to join us — either by signing up or
chipping in to help us win this race.

A simple way to frame it:
Christina is running to flip Michigan’s 10th — the John James seat. She
grew up here, she is raising her 3 kids here, and she was a special victims
prosecutor for 10 years.

This is the only open toss up seat in Michigan, it’s one of the most
competitive seats in the country, and Christina is the only Democrat
currently on the ballot - the other two don’t even have their signatures
collected. The way we win is by reaching people where they are and fighting
for our rights and freedoms!

*Then make the ask:*We’re building a strong field program, and it costs
about $250 a day. Ask folks to scan the QR code and give whatever they can.

This is about turning this moment into something real—conversations,
connections, and ultimately, votes.

If you can’t donate, ask them to sign up to door knock, write postcards,
phone/text bank, or host a meet and greet.. If they can’t sign up, thank
them for being there. Every interaction matters.

*If you're able to join us:*

Please text or email Sarah at 616-886-5174 or
sarah@christinahinesforcongress.com

Let’s show up and make it count.
See you out there!

--
Christina Hines
Candidate for Congress, MI-10

www.christinahinesforcongress.com
<http://www.christinahinesforcongress.com>

Friend,
No one in DC is fighting for working families like ours, and at a time when Republicans are spending money on war, cutting Medicaid, and making Americans sicker, I want to share why ensuring every American has access to healthcare is so personal for me.
Join me in fighting back to flip MI-10 and flip the House. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q1?refcode=x_260327_recipe_act]
DONATE TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q1?refcode=x_260327_recipe_act]
My mom, Lynda, was sick for most of my life growing up. That’s where my advocacy started. I know what it means to fight for care, for stability, and for dignity for family members who can’t always fight for themselves.
And I’m not alone. Every day, I speak to community members who need a little help because of life circumstances, an accident, or illness.
I feel very lucky that my oldest, Trey got to meet my mom. She passed away when he was two, while I was pregnant with Will and before Cece was even an idea! But my kiddos also know her through the stories we tell, the songs we sing, and the recipes I make. Cooking her food is one way I stay connected to her and remember the warmth she brought into our home. Her White Chicken Chili filled the house with that warmth and was a family favorite, feeding whoever sat at the table that night.
I would love to share a small part of her with you. Please feel free to print out this recipe and share a part of our family with yours.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/105767/images/1_6.jpg] [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/105767/images/2_5.jpg]
It's time we had a Congress full of people who are dedicated to taking care of people, rather than making it harder for families like ours to survive. Please consider supporting our campaign to help make that happen. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q1?refcode=x_260327_recipe_act]
SUPPORT OUR CAMPAIGN TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q1?refcode=x_260327_recipe_act]
Thank you for being part of this,
Christina

Republicans passed a bill to require eligibility tests more often, now once-a-quarter for many on Indiana Medicaid. The federal government already covers 90% of the costs for Medicaid. Hoosiers need Democrats in charge at the Statehouse who understand the importance of investments we make in Hoosier health now to the future of our state. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. This is on top of the 60,000 Hoosiers who already lost their coverage in December and January. Republicans passed a bill to require eligibility tests more often, now once-a-quarter for many on Indiana Medicaid. The federal government already covers 90% of the costs for Medicaid. Hoosiers need Democrats in charge at the Statehouse who understand the importance of investments we make in Hoosier health now to the future of our state. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. This included a proposal to give state utility regulators direct oversight and the ability to block sales of public utilities to private equity firms. I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won in 2024. Several ultra-MAGA opponents have entered the race. And GOP-aligned Super PACs are already spending millions attacking me.

Before you turn in: [**Can you split a $5 donation between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project before March 31 to help me win in Georgia?**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105591?t=6&akid=23385%2E878179%2En-beuM) | [CONTRIBUTE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105591?t=7&akid=23385%2E878179%2En-beuM)

| | Friends,
As we head into Convention, I'm proud to share that our campaign continues to earn strong support from those engaged in education across Michigan.
The College Republicans at [Oakland University](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001v1Xu6SwxuN4z763K1EAi31FhsIV8PraM8L5TvUS5q3hYj1n_WmU3BCWYCnk3TMjCd7gQq_H2P4xmM8eCde3SeyFPK_WEYYYKDjds_gwhBUU4zzz6NkiVWDRQH0pz_g-89LR7kVSug3LJboiYgL7-EHvN8sJe3txBwhJMlDhufRhuxoVJHTvbulsd2vscBnQhYuaOlTp-QfPXF6ICmuVjeQ==&c=-MXEqI-pLSE3iMt9TTmDFGM9ApYAnHyv_KNcOcF9dWB1fDrJiRYXFA==&ch=g666Ucc1Gzc8btggcSxwBpvjlGAwjBHp8tAwp5PNoe2y_EVNfbpwnw==) and [Western Michigan University](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001v1Xu6SwxuN4z763K1EAi31FhsIV8PraM8L5TvUS5q3hYj1n_WmU3BCWYCnk3TMjCnuM75iINP2Rqn6SkF8FDRpwAHpQNgOrKLMnRx8lR7i6ljIrWGLSkXD_0yzp4acLLuChl9CHyHuMSQuevROWstzID9UN-ZQbULWeOt5DAyVKUmTuBWR8jfIcFmJC9J_7HN4dT7P7ukL1p1iTBA3Rc0A==&c=-MXEqI-pLSE3iMt9TTmDFGM9ApYAnHyv_KNcOcF9dWB1fDrJiRYXFA==&ch=g666Ucc1Gzc8btggcSxwBpvjlGAwjBHp8tAwp5PNoe2y_EVNfbpwnw==) have both endorsed our campaign. These student leaders represent the next generation of Michigan voters who care deeply about the future of our state and the direction of our education system.
I'm also honored to have the support of [State Board of Education Member Nikki Snyder](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001v1Xu6SwxuN4z763K1EAi31FhsIV8PraM8L5TvUS5q3hYj1n_WmU3BCWYCnk3TMjCgQDAeOWPcTFJIVt918d5VJggVEINu-JBENfOQBDZB3M3fMR0Jx8f2c9s9T9iiIc29lANyP50ffcrqY7kE3FTM35E8x2K47Y2B5hJItY12w5HhHyzoPScCR5kGCsbwdkkI_szM6BqYepi5s-OfJ1HMA==&c=-MXEqI-pLSE3iMt9TTmDFGM9ApYAnHyv_KNcOcF9dWB1fDrJiRYXFA==&ch=g666Ucc1Gzc8btggcSxwBpvjlGAwjBHp8tAwp5PNoe2y_EVNfbpwnw==), a proven advocate for students and families who has consistently stood on principle and fought for accountability.
These endorsements matter. They reflect a growing coalition that understands something simple but important: protecting our education system and standing up for students requires more than rhetoric. It requires a commitment to the rule of law, fairness, and doing the job without political agendas.
While others may try to claim this issue as their own, the truth is that Michigan families deserve an Attorney General who will protect their rights, enforce the law, and ensure that every voice is heard.
That is the kind of leadership I will bring to this office.
Thank you for your continued support as we work toward victory this weekend.

Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: New Coast, Same Grind
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
Always love my time on the west coast. This week, I spent time in 3 cities in 3 days. I started in San Francisco on Saturday, Dana Point on Sunday, and finished in Los Angeles by Monday evening.
(I don't say this to brag about my frequent flyer miles but did hit Executive Platinum on American.)
Spoke with the next generation of veterans earning their Masters in Public Leadership at the University of San Francisco, teaching a public policy [https://bit.ly/4thwPcV] class alongside Kate Kranz Jordan [https://bit.ly/4tbKz8O] . Kate has done it all. As a Naval Academy grad/officer, she flew in the E-2C Hawkeyes off the USS Ronald Reagan, served on NATO's Rule of Law mission in Afghanistan, advised the Commander of US Naval Forces Europe, and co-authored a two-time LA Times bestseller about junior officers in the post-9/11 military & now a protocol officer in Spain.
In other words, she’s legit. Kate has makes real decisions under the exact conditions that most policy syllabi treat as case studies which is precisely why she belongs in front of a classroom. And the students were worthy of her. I left convinced the next generation of leaders is asking the right questions.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM%20USC.png]
Then on Sunday, I headed down to Dana Point for the 38th Annual Roth Conference — one of the largest small-cap investor gatherings in the country.
I also got to reconnect with Patrick Flood [https://bit.ly/4rX6W0Q] from [https://www.linkedin.com/company/ownersinhonor/] Owners in Honor [https://bit.ly/4rX6W0Q] , a true leader in the entrepreneurship through acquisition (ETA) space and someone who genuinely embodies what it means to build with purpose.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/CEO%20Session%20.png]
I wrapped my weekend up in LA for ALTSLA [https://bit.ly/48dOOsq] 2026 “the West Coast's premier alternative investment conference.” It was held at the InterContinental Downtown drawing CIOs, allocators, and fund managers from across the country.
In my keynote fireside chat, I shared the stage with alternative investments veteran Christopher Mears [https://bit.ly/4lSjUM5] , and discussed how geopolitical risk shapes business decisions. Given the state of the world, this was a timely conversation.
We spoke about Iran and the impact of the Strait of Hormuz’s closure, the downstream effects we’re already starting to see. It’s caused an energy shock, a supply chain rupture, and a war-risk insurance problem simultaneously. Even companies who don’t think they’re exposed to this issue likely have aspects of their portfolio that are.
The whole world is interconnected.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/LA%202026.png]
I’ve got lots more exciting travels and speaking engagements coming up. More to come.
Last night I appeared on CNN [https://bit.ly/4tg6EDq] with Erin Burnett and S.E. Cupp. Check it out [https://www.cnn.com/] here [http://CNN] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/CNN%20.png]
Thank you reading our newsletter. For more updates, please follow on Instagram [https://bit.ly/47s6mRv] and subscribe to my best-selling (31st in country) Substack [https://bit.ly/4te4VOV] for our weekly geopolitical and business analysis. Most importantly, please keep our troops and everyone in the region in your nightly prayers.
-Patrick

body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
Fellow Republicans,
Election Season is Here - Let's Get to Work
Campaigns are underway and the primary election is fast approaching. Our number one goal remains unchanging: elect Republicans in every possible race. While our tactics adapt to each phase of the election cycle, our commitment to victory remains steadfast. Our current focus is aggressive Get Out the Vote (GOTV) efforts and full support for all our Republican candidates up and down the ballot.
While winning elections is our immediate priority, it's critical we never lose sight of why these victories matter so much.
Republicans stand for limited government, individual freedom, fiscal responsibility, strong families, and traditional American values. Democrats offer a fundamentally different vision--one that relies more heavily on government expansion, higher taxes, and progressive social policies. Here are some clear examples:
Securing the border and enforcing immigration laws -- Republicans support stronger border security, reducing illegal crossings, and prioritizing legal immigration. These efforts protect wages, stem abuse of public services, and promote the rule of law.
Voter ID requirements -- Requiring photo identification to vote is a minimal requirement for election integrity and common sense; especially when ID checks are commonplace for everyday activities like buying alcohol or boarding a plane.
Banning biological males from competing in women's sports -- Protecting fair competition in female athletics by restricting participation based on biological sex. Republicans defend women's opportunities and safety, and advocate for "common sense" over gender ideology.
Law and order / backing the police -- Republicans support funding police, cracking down on crime, and restoring public safety (especially after recent spikes in certain cities). Republicans promote "back the blue," opposing "defund the police" movements, and emphasize prosecuting criminals over activist reforms.
Healthcare reforms focused on affordability and choice -- Republicans support price transparency, allowing cross-state insurance competition, reducing regulations that drive up costs, and targeting waste/fraud in programs like those found in Medicare/Medicaid.
In parallel with our election efforts, we continue vital organizational work: tracking County Party Conventions, helping previously unorganized counties stand up strong local parties, and monitoring leadership changes to strengthen our grassroots foundation statewide.
The NEGOP is also planning our State Convention and Vote Red Auction. Save the dates!
Thursday, June 5th: The exciting finale to our 2nd Annual Vote Red Auction & Dinner Friday, June 6th: Our State Convention in La Vista
These events are perfect opportunities to connect, celebrate, and build momentum heading into the general election.
Steady fundraising remains essential. Every dollar helps us keep the lights on, support our candidates, and deliver the results Nebraskans deserve.
It's easy to get caught up in the "how" of our daily work--calls, doors, meetings, and logistics. Let's stay energized and motivated by the "why."
Every action we take is building a stronger, freer, and more prosperous Nebraska under Republican leadership.
Stay involved, stay motivated, and let's deliver victories together!
For Nebraska, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| Update from Political Director Joe Hagerty...
GOTV is underway -- and we need all hands on deck.
The NEGOP and local county parties are going to be running door knocking days of action in key legislative districts across CD2, and between now and May 12th, our volunteers are the most important asset we have. We're on the ground connecting with Republican voters, making sure they know when, where, and how to vote in the Primary -- because an informed voter is a voter who actually shows up.
These legislative races are close. The margins are tight. And in cycles like this one, volunteer-driven turnout operations are what separate the wins from the near-misses. A few hours of your time between now and Primary Day can make a real difference for our candidates and for Nebraska.
Not sure where to vote or need to check your registration? Our number one goal remains unchanging: elect Republicans in every possible race. While our tactics adapt to each phase of the election cycle, our commitment to victory remains steadfast. Our current focus is aggressive Get Out the Vote (GOTV) efforts and full support for all our Republican candidates up and down the ballot. While winning elections is our immediate priority, it's critical we never lose sight of why these victories matter so much. Republicans stand for limited government, individual freedom, fiscal responsibility, strong families, and traditional American values. Democrats offer a fundamentally different vision--one that relies more heavily on government expansion, higher taxes, and progressive social policies. Here are some clear examples: Securing the border and enforcing immigration laws -- Republicans support stronger border security, reducing illegal crossings, and prioritizing legal immigration. These efforts protect wages, stem abuse of public services, and promote the rule of law. Voter ID requirements -- Requiring photo identification to vote is a minimal requirement for election integrity and common sense; especially when ID checks are commonplace for everyday activities like buying alcohol or boarding a plane. Banning biological males from competing in women's sports -- Protecting fair competition in female athletics by restricting participation based on biological sex. Republicans defend women's opportunities and safety, and advocate for "common sense" over gender ideology. Law and order / backing the police -- Republicans support funding police, cracking down on crime, and restoring public safety (especially after recent spikes in certain cities). Republicans promote "back the blue," opposing "defund the police" movements, and emphasize prosecuting criminals over activist reforms. Healthcare reforms focused on affordability and choice -- Republicans support price transparency, allowing cross-state insurance competition, reducing regulations that drive up costs, and targeting waste/fraud in programs like those found in Medicare/Medicaid. In parallel with our election efforts, we continue vital organizational work: tracking County Party Conventions, helping previously unorganized counties stand up strong local parties, and monitoring leadership changes to strengthen our grassroots foundation statewide. The NEGOP is also planning our State Convention and Vote Red Auction. Save the dates! Thursday, June 5th: The exciting finale to our 2nd Annual Vote Red Auction & Dinner Friday, June 6th: Our State Convention in La Vista These events are perfect opportunities to connect, celebrate, and build momentum heading into the general election. Steady fundraising remains essential. Every dollar helps us keep the lights on, support our candidates, and deliver the results Nebraskans deserve. It's easy to get caught up in the "how" of our daily work--calls, doors, meetings, and logistics. Let's stay energized and motivated by the "why." Every action we take is building a stronger, freer, and more prosperous Nebraska under Republican leadership. Stay involved, stay motivated, and let's deliver victories together! # **Trump becomes first sitting president to add signature to U.S. dollar bills in honor of 250th anniversary**
President Donald Trump is **[adding his signature to U.S. dollar bills](https://substack.com/redirect/73e861dc-7a3a-4603-8865-cd478426543d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the country's 250th anniversary, marking the first time a sitting president's signature will appear on paper currency, the Treasury Department announced Thursday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said "the President's mark on history as the architect of America's Golden Age economic revival is undeniable," calling the move "not only appropriate, but also well deserved."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/73e861dc-7a3a-4603-8865-cd478426543d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** U.S. paper currency has historically featured only the treasurer's and treasury secretary's signatures since first printed in 1861. A Trump-appointed federal commission also recently approved a design including Trump's image on 24-karat commemorative gold coins for the 250th anniversary, pending Treasury approval.

* **The pattern:** Adding his name to currency is Trump's latest effort to leave his mark on the federal government in new ways, with his name now affixed to the Kennedy Center, U.S. Institute of Peace, discount drug programs, savings accounts, and proposed warships. In 2020, Trump stamped his name onto Covid stimulus checks.

* * *
# **Iran lowers military recruitment age to 12, sparking international condemnation and memories of child soldiers in Iran-Iraq War**
The Iranian government **[announced Thursday](https://substack.com/redirect/a05cc9f2-942c-46b9-91ac-e4108b5e50fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** it has lowered the minimum age for military support roles to 12 years old through a new "For Iran" recruitment drive, with IRGC cultural official Rahim Nadali claiming a "high number" of young volunteers are eager to serve. Tehran residents report seeing teenagers in plainclothes wielding submachine guns at checkpoints, searching vehicles, and firing warning shots to control crowds following recent missile strikes, with recruits as young as 12 and 13 reportedly tasked with operational patrols, manning checkpoints, and gathering security data.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a05cc9f2-942c-46b9-91ac-e4108b5e50fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The move stands in direct violation of Article 38 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, which mandates states ensure those under 15 do not take part in hostilities. During the 1980s Iran-Iraq War, the regime deployed a paramilitary force of 12-17 year olds in "human wave" attacks to clear Iraqi minefields with their bodies, reportedly issuing many children plastic "Keys to Paradise" promising immediate entry into heaven upon martyrdom--an estimated 36,000 to 45,000 students were killed.
* **The backdrop:** The recruitment drive follows a period where security forces killed over 200 children during early 2026 protests, according to the Center for Human Rights in Iran. With over three million child laborers already in the country and a history of glorifying child martyrs like Hossein Fahmideh in school textbooks, activists warn lowering the recruitment age is "not a response to volunteerism, but a calculated move to further militarize Iran's youth and use them as expendable tools of the state."

* * *
# **Yemen 's Houthi rebels threaten to open new Red Sea front against US and Israel in coordination with Iran**
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Thursday they are "fully militarily ready with all options" **[to stand with Iran against the US and Israel,](https://substack.com/redirect/2be362ab-0bdd-4225-989e-427aed88e933?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** threatening to open a new front along the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab Strait--a key global trade route. A Houthi leader told Reuters the group is in "direct coordination with Iran," saying "until now Iran is doing well and is defeating the enemy every day and the battle is going in its direction. If anything contrary to this happens then we can assess."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2be362ab-0bdd-4225-989e-427aed88e933?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The Houthis' involvement directly threatens the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a 20-mile wide passage southwest of Yemen connecting the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, where $1 trillion worth of goods pass annually between Europe and Asia. The rebels previously waged war along the passage during the Israel-Hamas war, sowing "chaos and disruptions" at the key trade route. Any attacks would further risk shipments from Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, which has been redirecting barrels through the Red Sea following the Strait of Hormuz closure.
* **The escalation:** Iran issued a direct threat Wednesday to take the Bab al-Mandab Strait if the US invades Kharg Island, with IRGC sources telling Tasnim News Agency "Iran has both the will and the ability to create a completely credible threat against it." Tehran and Washington continue trading threats as thousands of US soldiers deploy to the Middle East, with President Trump refusing to rule out a ground invasion of Iran.

* * *
# **Senate unanimously advances deal to reopen most of DHS after 42-day shutdown, but excludes ICE and CBP funding**
The Senate unanimously **[advanced a deal early Friday morning](https://substack.com/redirect/bcd6540e-1d4c-4378-8423-9b5ecd97a78f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to reopen most of the Department of Homeland Security after a 42-day shutdown sparked by the Trump administration's immigration operations in Minnesota, largely giving Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer what he wanted--no funding for ICE and parts of CBP. Senate Majority Leader John Thune said "this is what they were willing to agree to" but argued Democrats "got no reforms on DHS, which they could have had if they had been willing to work with us," while Schumer declared "this is exactly what we wanted" and praised his caucus for holding the line.
* **Why it matters:** The deal mirrors previous Democratic attempts to pass legislation carving out immigration funding but lacks the stringent reforms Democrats desired, like requiring judicial warrants or requiring agents to unmask. However, ICE and CBP remain "flush with roughly $75 billion in cash from Trump's 'big, beautiful bill,'" giving agencies a buffer, with Thune saying Republicans "anticipated this a year ago" and "pre-loaded up" funding because "we anticipated this was likely going to happen."
* **What 's next:** The deal heads to the House, where Republicans aren't enthusiastic about not funding key components of Trump's immigration crackdown. Sen. Eric Schmitt said Democrats "are trying to shut down ICE funding for the remainder of the fiscal year -- ultimately they won't be successful" and he'll push "to lock in funding for deportation operations and salaries for a decade" through the party-line reconciliation process, though Republicans want to include SAVE Act portions and Iran war funding, which some worry may be difficult given strict Senate rules.

However, ICE and CBP remain "flush with roughly $75 billion in cash from Trump's 'big, beautiful bill,'" giving agencies a buffer, with Thune saying Republicans "anticipated this a year ago" and "pre-loaded up" funding because "we anticipated this was likely going to happen." What 's next: The deal heads to the House, where Republicans aren't enthusiastic about not funding key components of Trump's immigration crackdown. Sen. Eric Schmitt said Democrats "are trying to shut down ICE funding for the remainder of the fiscal year -- ultimately they won't be successful" and he'll push "to lock in funding for deportation operations and salaries for a decade" through the party-line reconciliation process, though Republicans want to include SAVE Act portions and Iran war funding, which some worry may be difficult given strict Senate rules. name: Jon Ossoff
subject: Good morning, Peter

body:
#

Peter,
As I travel across Georgia, more and more people of every background and belief tell me their stories and share their frustration about the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration.
_I spoke to a cotton grower here in Georgia about the skyrocketing prices of fertilizer and diesel caused by the war._
_I spoke to a woman in her early 60s who waits tables for a living. She’s fighting cancer. She told me she was going to lose her health coverage in the middle of chemotherapy because Trump refused to extend ACA tax credits._
***
And it’s not just Democrats and independents sharing these stories. *Republicans* take me aside, or they call me on the phone.
They tell me they’re afraid of where this President has taken us, and they don’t want it to go on.
They tell me they’re voting for a Democrat for the first time!
And it’s no mystery why: this is the cruelest and most arrogant group of people who have ever ascended to high office, and their cruelty and their arrogance are matched only by their incompetence.
***
**But it doesn’t have to be this way.**
Everywhere I go, across our state, people also tell me they are desperate for change and for new ideas.
_The student working through college who still needs food stamps to make rent, whose conscience can’t stand their tax dollars being used to lock up immigrant children here at home._
_The South Georgia farmer whose costs rise and earnings fall each year, whose kids have left the family farm, who’s still waiting for federal aid long after the storm._
_The young couple expecting their first child — who worry how they’ll afford a crib and a stroller, let alone a first home — whose health insurance just went up a thousand dollars per month._
***
I believe we can reform our corrupt politics. I believe we will escape this moral tailspin and recommit ourselves to the values that have made this country great.
But none of this is possible without victory this November, and the battle is already on. Georgia is the most crucial battleground state in the country, and this will be the tightest and hardest-fought U.S. Senate race this year.
[**So, Peter, I’m asking for your help. Will you donate $25 to my reelection campaign today? This is something you can do right now to make a real difference.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260327-1-f&t=1&akid=1964%2E5691347%2EJ2tNLl)
