Sammy's Law, a bipartisan bill currently making its way through Congress, aims to protect children on social media platforms by allowing parental safety apps to monitor minors' accounts and flag concerning behavior. The legislation is named after Sammy Chapman, a 16-year-old who died from a fentanyl overdose after being approached by a drug dealer on Snapchat.

Sen. Katie Britt, one of the bill's sponsors released a statement saying, "As parents and legislators, it’s our job to protect our children and teens—our most vulnerable—in every way we can. In the age of social media and the challenges that come with it, Sammy’s Law is a critical step towards protecting our children online by ensuring parents have access to the necessary tools to keep their children safe.”

Derek, this is urgent:
**There’s a case before the Supreme Court right now that could PROHIBIT states from counting legally cast mail-in ballots – potentially disenfranchising millions of voters in the midterm elections.**

Peter, For five weeks now, Donald Trump has been manufacturing a crisis at our airports. He shut down the Department of Homeland Security, and chose not to pay TSA officials with the slush fund provided to DHS by the Big Ugly Bill, forcing approximately 500 to resign to find other employment. Then, as lines grew increasingly longer, President Trump still wouldn’t fund TSA and instead sent the same unqualified, unvetted, untrained, lawless ICE agents that have been terrorizing our cities to our airports, fomenting more chaos and fear. And Peter, we need to be clear about something: this is not incompetence. This is an intentional strategy. **Donald Trump sees this crisis as leverage. He is refusing to restore TSA funding unless Congress passes his voter suppression law, the SAVE Act. Read that again: he is refusing to pay TSA officers and causing hours-long waits at airports just so he can try to force passage of a law designed to make it harder for you to vote.** It will not work. The SAVE Act is not about election security — it is a deliberate effort to disenfranchise millions of American voters. This bill doesn’t solve a single real problem. It was crafted solely to rig the rules in Republicans’ favor. And while Trump plays these political games, real people are paying the price. The lines at airport security keep getting longer, and the dedicated public servants who work for DHS — _except ICE agents_ — are not getting paid. They are taking on second jobs, relying on food banks, and struggling to make ends meet while Donald Trump uses their livelihoods as a bargaining chip. Here’s the thing, Peter: this could all be resolved today. Democrats have offered a simple solution — carve ICE out and rein in the abuses of Trump’s immigration crackdown and we can fund the rest of DHS. But Trump won’t allow it. clean_body: | Peter, For five weeks now, Donald Trump has been manufacturing a crisis at our airports. He shut down the Department of Homeland Security, and chose not to pay TSA officials with the slush fund provided to DHS by the Big Ugly Bill, forcing approximately 500 to resign to find other employment. Then, as lines grew increasingly longer, President Trump still wouldn’t fund TSA and instead sent the same unqualified, unvetted, untrained, lawless ICE agents that have been terrorizing our cities to our airports, fomenting more chaos and fear. And Peter, we need to be clear about something: this is not incompetence. This is an intentional strategy. Donald Trump sees this crisis as leverage. He is refusing to restore TSA funding unless Congress passes his voter suppression law, the SAVE Act. Read that again: he is refusing to pay TSA officers and causing hours-long waits at airports just so he can try to force passage of a law designed to make it harder for you to vote. It will not work. The SAVE Act is not about election security — it is a deliberate effort to disenfranchise millions of American voters. This bill doesn’t solve a single real problem. It was crafted solely to rig the rules in Republicans’ favor. And while Trump plays these political games, real people are paying the price. The lines at airport security keep getting longer, and the dedicated public servants who work for DHS — except ICE agents — are not getting paid. They are taking on second jobs, relying on food banks, and struggling to make ends meet while Donald Trump uses their livelihoods as a bargaining chip. Here’s the thing, Peter: this could all be resolved today. Democrats have offered a simple solution — carve ICE out and rein in the abuses of Trump’s immigration crackdown and we can fund the rest of DHS. But Trump won’t allow it. Hi team,
A local business owner asked me to come see him this week. I drove 30 minutes to his office, only for him to tell me he didn't know why I was running because I couldn't win.
He's not from around here, and I could tell.
People who refuse to try. People who bury their heads in the sand. People who tell others there's no sense in working to make a change. **That 's not who we are.**
On the campaign trail, I've met amazing people from our part of the state. The mom who advocates for programs for kids with autism. The hunter who teaches others not just how to hunt but how to appreciate the beauty of the outdoors. The woman who goes to every county commissioners' meeting to make sure they don't forget about Tremont. The retired guy who organized his community to keep a data center from coming in and [ruining Montour Preserve](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4d8d2276-0311-4c60-b09d-62cf857da9a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We're fighting for our communities - and for people like the guy I met with who feel like we just have to accept the way things are. For people who feel angry when others point out that the status quo is no good.
And there's no question about that. Not when we have a Congressman who has doubled his own wealth representing us, while not even holding a single town hall.
So to everyone who has ignored our district, shrugged us off, and decided we weren't worth the investment or the effort - we're here to prove you wrong.
**In the last four years, the counties in this district shifted an average of 33 points to the left.**
Because people here are tired of getting left behind while their representatives get rich. They're sick of their health care getting cut while billionaires get another tax break. They're done with Dan Meuser hopping on a plane and saying "get over it" while our communities are in crisis.
We're ready for something different. For a movement that actually does the work - shows up, listens, and then makes the government work for us. Our campaign is proving that.
We have the momentum, the message, and the coalition to finally flip this seat.
That's why Meuser ran off to Florida last week to host a two-day fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago. **He 's scared of us.** He knows that if we keep growing this movement, his time in Congress is over. So let's keep this up.
**Our end-of-quarter deadline is almost here, and everyone will be watching when our numbers go public. Let 's show them that Meuser is right to be scared. PA-09 is ready for something better.**
**[Can you chip in today?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d95bf4df-1a7d-4f99-a2b8-254dc1f1a94c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thanks for being a part of this. Everything we've built so far is because of your support, and I don't take that for granted.
- Rachel Wallace

clean_body: - Michele Tafoya here! I never really considered running for office. Ever. I was too focused on raising my family, and being the best football sideline reporter I could be. But even in the last few weeks, Minnesota has become the embodiment of everything wrong with politics today. Tim Walz, his inner circle, and the corrupt political class are too busy: Wasting billions of our tax dollars on fraudulent daycares Failing to condemn the activists storming churches Raising prices on hardworking families Sabotaging anything the President wants to do Forcing men into women's spaces Pitting Americans against each other I can 't sit on the sidelines anymore. That's why I'm throwing my hat in the ring and announcing my candidacy for U.S. Senate! thought long and hard about the dynamics of this race before jumping in. Minnesota has long been considered simply out of reach for Republicans. The last time it voted for a GOP President was Nixon. The pundits and political experts say a Republican could never win here. But this year is going to be different for three key reasons: FIRST - I'm running against Tim Walz's right hand. All the rampant fraud that took place here happened under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as it did under his. We will remind voters about that fact every single day. SECOND - The President has increased his voter share each time he has run. He nearly flipped this state in the last election, and Kamala Harris' running mate was our sitting Governor! Momentum is on our side. THIRD - I'm a different kind of candidate, and I know how to win. I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said. In my years on the sidelines, I 've seen a LOT of underdogs win football games that the "experts" said were impossible. The Minnesota Senate race will be another chapter in that storied history. | | ---|--- Thanks in advance for your support. body:
Team Hong at No Kings
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260327-2658)
Peter,
Tomorrow is No Kings Day — and Team Hong is showing up.
Across the country, over 3,000 communities are gathering for what organizers say could be one of the largest single days of nonviolent protest in American history. Right here in Wisconsin, nearly 100 rallies and marches are planned, from Siren to Sturgeon Bay to downtown Madison.
We're in the streets because enough is enough. There’s an illegal war driving up costs and putting us in danger. We’ve endured endless attacks on our freedoms. We’re living under a regime that answers to billionaires while working families can't afford groceries.
The message of No Kings Day is the same message at the center of this campaign: In America, the power belongs to the people.
So that’s why tomorrow, Team Hong isn't just marching. We're organizing.
Volunteers have stepped up across Wisconsin to lead canvasses at No Kings rallies this weekend. We’ll be registering people to vote, educating voters on what’s at stake in the upcoming elections, and sharing Fran’s message of permanent affordability.
Look for us in the following cities:
* [Appleton](https://act.francescahong.com/go/10240?t=1&akid=2658%2E105371%2ECoCv25)

Peter ,
460,000 Virginians have already cast ballots in the redistricting referendum – the one that could redraw the congressional map and wipe out most of the GOP’s safe seats.
At first glance, those early numbers might look encouraging for Democrats.
They shouldn’t.
Early voting is only one slice of the electorate, and it can create a false sense of security. The voters who show up on Election Day in low-turnout contests like this – irregular voters – can change the outcome fast.
That is the whole challenge in Virginia right now.
The people most likely to decide this referendum are probably not the people who have already voted. They are the ones still sitting on the sidelines, who we need to contact again and again before they move, and that’s exactly what we do at GOTV PAC.
April 21 is now just 25 days away – this is the stretch where turnout programs either close the gap or lose the race.

name: Leah Donahey, LCV
subject: TAKE ACTION: Tax Big Oil’s Windfall Profits!
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1OTEyODcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQyMTE0OTg0NgS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Tell Congress:
Pass The Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act!

It’s time for Congress to pass the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act. Time and time again, we’ve seen Big Oil profits skyrocket during crises in
oil-rich regions — and we’re feeling the pain now. Oil prices are surging and
the Big Oil companies that bankrolled Trump’s campaign are poised to rake in record
profits.

A recent analysis estimates that the oil industry could make over $60 billion in
additional profits this year. And who foots the bill? The working families who
are already struggling to make ends meet.

The Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act would ensure that Big Oil’s exorbitant
profits generated by price gauging are returned back to the American people,
rather than further enriching oil and gas corporations, their wealthy
shareholders, and billionaire CEOs.

Tell Congress to support the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act today! https://links.messages.lcv. ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/04wrM8Gp_ Peter, Time and time again, we’ve seen Big Oil profits skyrocket during crises in
oil-rich regions. As billionaire oil and gas CEOs get richer, it is everyday
people who bear the highest costs — human, environmental, and economic — of war.
It’s high time Big Oil pays for its profiteering. Since the war in Iran began last month, oil prices have continued to surge and
the Big Oil companies that bankrolled Trump’s campaign are poised to rake in record
profits. A recent analysis estimates that the oil industry could make over $60 billion in additional profits this year, while the average family in America will pay over $900 more for gasoline compared to before the war. And that number continues to grow. That’s why we’re calling on Congress to pass the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax
Act.Led by Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse and Rep. Ro Khanna, this bill would ensure that
the exorbitant profits generated by wartime price gauging are returned back to
the American people, rather than further enriching oil and gas corporations,
their wealthy shareholders, and billionaire CEOs. Join LCV in calling on Congress to pass The Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act! https://links.messages.lcv. For more than a year, communities have been feeling the pain of Trump’s broken
promises. Energy costs were already unaffordable before the war began, and now working families’ wallets are taking
an even greater hit: In 2024, Trump campaigned on a promise to cut gas prices in half. Instead, he started a war that sent crude oil past $110 a barrel. In 2025, Trump’s insistence on dirty oil, gas, and coal drove up electric bills by 13%. Now, with prices rising daily, Trump continues to block clean, affordable energy — like wind and solar — here at home. It’s time to usher in a new era of accountability for Trump and Big Oil’s
corporate greed. Take action today and support the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act. https://links.messages.lcv. As long as the U.S. remains dependent on fossil fuels, working families will
keep paying the price — not only shrinking our wallets, but also our health,
safety, and future. The solution is building clean energy close to home,
creating power sources that lower costs, create jobs, and that are sustainable
for our communities and our climate. Thank you for taking action with LCV — for people and for our planet. Leah Donahey

subject: This is better than a strongly worded letter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
People want Democrats to show up.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260327-2&t=1&akid=3300%2E587540%2EL-8LN1)
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260327_2_nate.0EpldZ&refcode=em20260327-3300&t=2&akid=3300%2E587540%2EL-8LN1)
Peter,
Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidate **Nate Blouin** just went on the Rachel Maddow show on MSNBC to talk about a planned ICE detention facility in Utah and how the community around Salt Lake City is coming together to fight back.
**Nate is leading that fight.** He introduced the "ICE Out" bill in the Utah legislature to limit ICE's ability to operate in the state, and he's shown up to protests outside the facility, standing shoulder to shoulder with hundreds of Salt Lake City residents to stop the new detention center — all before he's even become a member of Congress.
The action Nate is taking locally and the national attention he’s bringing to the issue is exactly the kind of leadership that people want to see in Congress. They don’t want more strongly worded letters from people with power to do something. They want Democrats to show up and actually fight, _win or lose_ , for what’s right.
**Nate is running for Congress in Utah** — and his opponent in the race has taken tens of thousands of dollars in contributions from private prison corporations.
Meanwhile, _Nate doesn’t accept any donations from corporate PACs_ at all. Just like every Leaders-backed candidate, he is funded by grassroots supporters like you.
We’re working every day to elect inspiring leaders like Nate because we believe that the future will be written by the young progressives we elect to office now.
**[Will you pitch in $5 now to help us support Nate Blouin and more game-changing leaders like him?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260327_2_nate.0EpldZ&refcode=em20260327-3300&amount=5&t=3&akid=3300%2E587540%2EL-8LN1)**

Thank you,
Leaders We Deserve

clean_body: Anyone who’s read the news this month can probably infer that Republicans are in serious trouble Anyone who’s read the news this month can probably infer that Republicans are in serious trouble | | | | | Peter, 🚨 OUR FUNDRAISING HAS HIT A SNAG 🚨 Can you spare $32, Peter? That 's our average donation in March so far -- and it's exactly what it will take to help us stay competitive and keep Texas red. Our fundraising has fallen off, and honestly, it's happening at a TERRIBLE time. We're preparing to report our 1st quarter fundraising numbers to the FEC, and we can't leave a single penny on the table. By now, you've probably heard: Republicans are in serious trouble here in Texas. Earlier this month, Democrats turned out in massive numbers, more than Republicans for the first time in recent memory, with over 2.3 million casting ballots in their Senate primary. Radical James Talarico emerged as their nominee, fresh off raising millions in record time, and national Democrats are already pouring in cash to make him competitive and flip the Lone Star State blue. They want to erase everything we've built here and end our 32-year winning streak for the first time since 1994. We cannot let that happen. So far this month, 430 conservatives have chipped in, averaging $32 each. It's not going to be enough to help us finish out the first quarter. That's why I'm imploring you to help me today. If we don't remain competitive, it could be the end of the line for Republicans in Texas. Can you make a $32 contribution right now? It would mean so much to us. Peter, I don't want to fight alone. If it's been a while since you've donated, I understand. But if you still believe in what we've fought for -- secure borders, tax relief, strong judges, and keeping Texas red -- I'm asking you to show up today. Your $32 will enable me to keep fighting for Texas values while pushing back against the radical left. Your name on our donor list shows we're not fighting alone. Thousands of grassroots donors pledging our average March donation sends a powerful message:Conservative Republicans are energized and unshaken -- and we will not let our streak end. I'm in this fight to keep Texas red and bring common sense back to Washington. Please stand with me in this critical moment. Thank you, Ted Cruz U.S. Senator (R-TX) | | | Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate | | PO Box 25400 Houston, TX 77265 | | | |

---
**Boysko Bulletin: Back Home in District 38**
---
Dear Peter, We gaveled out on March 16th, ending the 2026 General Assembly Session for now. We will return for reconvene to vote on the Governor’s amendments and vetoes, if any, on April 22nd and then stay for a [special session](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128212615/610602719/-755369062?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmE4NjczODctMzcyYS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NcSgs0pg6yqs0-d_70KnTDa9VIkCVX8cTzwcA7AbX0=&emci=548c8439-6d1d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=ba867387-372a-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556) to finish the budget. The Senate and the House of Delegates need more time to discuss the major revenue sources for this biennium budget. A major issue is whether the tax exemption for data centers should end before its existing expiration date to be used to serve as this source. It was a very successful session for me, passing policy initiatives that I have championed over the past decade, reflecting many years of effort with advocates and my colleagues. Thanks to all of you who voted for Governor Spanberger, I expect that the bills will be signed into law by Governor Spanberger rather than being vetoed as was their fate in the prior Administration. We have learned many lessons over the past decade - one important lesson is that when we use our voting power, we can make positive change. We can ensure that our Government protects the most vulnerable of our community members, protects our freedoms, and provides the opportunity for education for all, good jobs and working conditions, safe and affordable housing and transportation and more. When we pool our resources for the public good, we all benefit. SB2 passed! I am very proud of my work on Paid Family and Medical Leave legislation - work will begin this summer to build an insurance program that will provide up to 12 weeks of paid leave for serious medical crises, care of a new baby, and deployment. No longer will working Virginians be forced to choose between a pay check or caring for themselves or a loved one. The United States is the ONLY industrialized nation in the world without any sort of paid leave program at the federal level. Now, we will join the other 13 states and the District of Columbia in providing that benefit for Virginians. SB215 passed! I am also pleased that the bill I’ve carried since the 2017 Session to narrow the wage gap has passed. Employers will no longer base wage decisions for new hires on salary history - a practice that locks people into low paying wages, often earned when combining work with caregiving or school or academic jobs. We will all benefit when all of our community members earn a fair wage. Yesterday was Equal Pay Day, representing how far into the year women working full-time, year-round have to work to earn as much as their white, non-Hispanic male counterparts did the previous year. SB335 passed! I am also very proud of the work we have done to make the criminal justice system fairer for people with disabilities. Working closely since 2020 with those who fight for a life like ours for our community members with disabilities including autism and mental illness, this legislation will keep people who’ve had a crisis out of prison if their interaction with law enforcement was the result of their disability. SB348 passed! I’ve also been fighting for a safe firearm storage bill for several years - frustrated and heartbroken by the stories of adults who come home from work and lay their firearm on a table or counter, turning their back for just a minute - long enough for a child to pick it up and shoot themself or another family member. These are tragic stories, preventable by locking up firearms in a safe. We have tax credits for firearm safes that are sufficient to cover their cost. You can see below the [full slate of bills](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128212616/610602720/-1447329927?q=eyJzZWxlY3RlZFBhdHJvblR5cGUiOlsxXSwic2VsZWN0ZWRQYXRyb24iOjUyLCJzZWxlY3RlZFNlc3Npb24iOjU5LCJpbmNsdWRlRmFpbGVkIjp0cnVlfQ==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmE4NjczODctMzcyYS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NcSgs0pg6yqs0-d_70KnTDa9VIkCVX8cTzwcA7AbX0=&emci=548c8439-6d1d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=ba867387-372a-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=22486556) that I carried. I will be back in Richmond on April 22 for the Reconvene Session where we vote on the Governor’s actions on our bills. Then I will stay for a special session to finish work on the budget. As a member of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee, I spent many hours weighing the requests for amendments to the budget proposed by the prior Administration. Our work was made far more difficult by the actions of the federal Administration which have impacted our healthcare system, our ability to feed our most vulnerable, and K-12 and higher education. I am very grateful for the advocates who met with me and my staff to explain their work - we are very fortunate in Virginia to have so many gifted healthcare workers, social workers, environmentalists, teachers, transportation experts and others working on our behalf. Meanwhile, back in our community, we are very busy. We face many challenges as a result of the actions of the federal government. One of the most concerning is that they have taken action that threatens to undermine the fairness of our fall elections. The President has convinced Texas and other states to redraw their Congressional maps to ensure a stronger MAGA Trump-supporting majority at the federal level. Here in Virginia, we have taken action to respond by embarking on our own temporary redistricting effort. I am working on the campaign to educate voters on why a YES vote is the best way to fight for our democracy. A "yes" vote would allow the General Assembly to redraw Virginia's congressional districts for a temporary period of time, as a direct response to the other states who have done so, in addition to giving effect to the proposed district map in time for the 2026 Congressional elections and return the responsibility of drawing the congressional districts in 2031 to the Virginia Redistricting Commission. A "no" vote would not allow Virginia to respond, letting other states and the current MAGA president hold control over Congress. Please be aware that there are mailers and false advertisements advising people to vote no using photos of President Obama and Governor Spanberger. I’ve included more information below regarding the scam and also on volunteer opportunities and early voting. See you at a town hall or out in our community soon! Kindest regards,
---

Jennifer B. Boysko Member, Senate of VirginiaRepresenting the 38th Senate District making up the northernmost portions of Fairfax County (Great Falls, Herndon, McLean, Reston, Wolf Trap, parts of unincorporated Vienna and a slice of Falls Church) PS If you would like to support my work, please visit [my fundraising page](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128212617/610602721/1617457950?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmE4NjczODctMzcyYS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NcSgs0pg6yqs0-d_70KnTDa9VIkCVX8cTzwcA7AbX0=). **Photo Gallery**

The Governor’s Fellows Program is a prestigious opportunity for rising college seniors, recent college graduates, and postgraduate students to gain firsthand experience in the executive branch of state government. During their time in service to the Commonwealth, Governor’s fellows have the opportunity to learn from special guest speakers who are leaders in state government and beyond. Fellows also experience state government on the road, visiting state government agencies and historic sites that have shaped our past and are improving our future. “This fellowship is a unique opportunity to attract emerging professionals, assist in the development of the early stages of their professional journeys, and expose them to state government career pathways,” said Secretary of Administration Traci J. Deshazor. “I’ve had the pleasure of working with Governor’s fellows in previous administrations, and I know firsthand how rewarding and impactful this eight-week experience can be.” To apply, visit the Governor’s Fellows Program website. Qualified applicants must be rising college seniors, graduating seniors, or graduate students. All Virginia college and university students are eligible to apply. Virginia residents who attend out-of-state colleges and universities are also eligible. Both public and private college and university students are encouraged to apply. The deadline to apply for the Governor’s Fellows Program is April 10, 2026. Interviews will begin on April 21, 2026. Applicants will be advised on decisions beginning on April 30, 2026. The program runs from June 8, 2026 through July 31, 2026.

Founded in 2013 by Ozlem Goker-Alpan, the Lysosomal & Rare Disorders Research & Treatment Center is a leader in advancing care and research for lysosomal diseases and other rare genetic disorders. With more than two decades of dedication to patients living with rare diseases, Dr. Goker-Alpan has helped position the Center at the forefront of innovation, discovery, and compassionate care. The Center is committed to expanding our understanding of these complex conditions by studying the biological pathways behind them, improving methods of diagnosis, and developing more effective treatments. Through cutting-edge research and patient-centered care, the Center works to bring new hope to individuals and families affected by rare diseases. Their vision is to create a future where lysosomal disorders are no longer a barrier to living a full and healthy life. By supporting patients both across the United States and internationally, the Center strives to improve quality of life, advance medical breakthroughs, and ensure that every patient has access to the care and support they deserve. clean_body: | | | Boysko Bulletin: Back Home in District 38 Dear Peter, We gaveled out on March 16th, ending the 2026 General Assembly Session for now. We will return for reconvene to vote on the Governor’s amendments and vetoes, if any, on April 22nd and then stay for a to finish the budget. The Senate and the House of Delegates need more time to discuss the major revenue sources for this biennium budget. A major issue is whether the tax exemption for data centers should end before its existing expiration date to be used to serve as this source. It was a very successful session for me, passing policy initiatives that I have championed over the past decade, reflecting many years of effort with advocates and my colleagues. Thanks to all of you who voted for Governor Spanberger, I expect that the bills will be signed into law by Governor Spanberger rather than being vetoed as was their fate in the prior Administration. We have learned many lessons over the past decade - one important lesson is that when we use our voting power, we can make positive change. We can ensure that our Government protects the most vulnerable of our community members, protects our freedoms, and provides the opportunity for education for all, good jobs and working conditions, safe and affordable housing and transportation and more. When we pool our resources for the public good, we all benefit. SB2 passed! I am very proud of my work on Paid Family and Medical Leave legislation - work will begin this summer to build an insurance program that will provide up to 12 weeks of paid leave for serious medical crises, care of a new baby, and deployment. No longer will working Virginians be forced to choose between a pay check or caring for themselves or a loved one. The United States is the ONLY industrialized nation in the world without any sort of paid leave program at the federal level. Now, we will join the other 13 states and the District of Columbia in providing that benefit for Virginians. SB215 passed! I am also pleased that the bill I’ve carried since the 2017 Session to narrow the wage gap has passed. Employers will no longer base wage decisions for new hires on salary history - a practice that locks people into low paying wages, often earned when combining work with caregiving or school or academic jobs. We will all benefit when all of our community members earn a fair wage. Yesterday was Equal Pay Day, representing how far into the year women working full-time, year-round have to work to earn as much as their white, non-Hispanic male counterparts did the previous year. SB335 passed! I am also very proud of the work we have done to make the criminal justice system fairer for people with disabilities. Working closely since 2020 with those who fight for a life like ours for our community members with disabilities including autism and mental illness, this legislation will keep people who’ve had a crisis out of prison if their interaction with law enforcement was the result of their disability. SB348 passed! I’ve also been fighting for a safe firearm storage bill for several years - frustrated and heartbroken by the stories of adults who come home from work and lay their firearm on a table or counter, turning their back for just a minute - long enough for a child to pick it up and shoot themself or another family member. These are tragic stories, preventable by locking up firearms in a safe. We have tax credits for firearm safes that are sufficient to cover their cost. You can see below the that I carried. I will be back in Richmond on April 22 for the Reconvene Session where we vote on the Governor’s actions on our bills. Then I will stay for a special session to finish work on the budget. As a member of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee, I spent many hours weighing the requests for amendments to the budget proposed by the prior Administration. Our work was made far more difficult by the actions of the federal Administration which have impacted our healthcare system, our ability to feed our most vulnerable, and K-12 and higher education. I am very grateful for the advocates who met with me and my staff to explain their work - we are very fortunate in Virginia to have so many gifted healthcare workers, social workers, environmentalists, teachers, transportation experts and others working on our behalf. Meanwhile, back in our community, we are very busy. We face many challenges as a result of the actions of the federal government. One of the most concerning is that they have taken action that threatens to undermine the fairness of our fall elections. The President has convinced Texas and other states to redraw their Congressional maps to ensure a stronger MAGA Trump-supporting majority at the federal level. Here in Virginia, we have taken action to respond by embarking on our own temporary redistricting effort. I am working on the campaign to educate voters on why a YES vote is the best way to fight for our democracy. A "yes" vote would allow the General Assembly to redraw Virginia's congressional districts for a temporary period of time, as a direct response to the other states who have done so, in addition to giving effect to the proposed district map in time for the 2026 Congressional elections and return the responsibility of drawing the congressional districts in 2031 to the Virginia Redistricting Commission. A "no" vote would not allow Virginia to respond, letting other states and the current MAGA president hold control over Congress. Please be aware that there are mailers and false advertisements advising people to vote no using photos of President Obama and Governor Spanberger. I’ve included more information below regarding the scam and also on volunteer opportunities and early voting. See you at a town hall or out in our community soon! Kindest regards, Jennifer B. But this is not the end of the fight. The bill now heads to , and there is still time for Virginians to make their voices heard. Our community has been clear: a casino in Tysons is not the right path for Fairfax County. The Governor’s Fellows Program is a prestigious opportunity for rising college seniors, recent college graduates, and postgraduate students to gain firsthand experience in the executive branch of state government. During their time in service to the Commonwealth, Governor’s fellows have the opportunity to learn from special guest speakers who are leaders in state government and beyond. Fellows also experience state government on the road, visiting state government agencies and historic sites that have shaped our past and are improving our future. “This fellowship is a unique opportunity to attract emerging professionals, assist in the development of the early stages of their professional journeys, and expose them to state government career pathways,” said Secretary of Administration Traci J. Deshazor. “I’ve had the pleasure of working with Governor’s fellows in previous administrations, and I know firsthand how rewarding and impactful this eight-week experience can be.” To apply, visit the Governor’s Fellows Program website. Qualified applicants must be rising college seniors, graduating seniors, or graduate students. All Virginia college and university students are eligible to apply. Virginia residents who attend out-of-state colleges and universities are also eligible. Both public and private college and university students are encouraged to apply. The deadline to apply for the Governor’s Fellows Program is April 10, 2026. Interviews will begin on April 21, 2026. Applicants will be advised on decisions beginning on April 30, 2026. The program runs from June 8, 2026 through July 31, 2026. If you're a displaced federal worker or contractor trying to figure out what comes next, this day is for you. Not a job fair, not a networking event, is a full-day, working summit designed to help you translate your experience into your next opportunity and leave with an actual plan. You'll choose one of two tracks based on the move you hope to make — Public & Civic Sector (state/local government, nonprofits, education, human services) or Private Sector & Entrepreneurship (consulting, corporate, tech, freelance) — and spend the day in focused sessions tailored to that path. Give Back Founded in 2013 by Ozlem Goker-Alpan, the Lysosomal & Rare Disorders Research & Treatment Center is a leader in advancing care and research for lysosomal diseases and other rare genetic disorders. With more than two decades of dedication to patients living with rare diseases, Dr. Goker-Alpan has helped position the Center at the forefront of innovation, discovery, and compassionate care. The Center is committed to expanding our understanding of these complex conditions by studying the biological pathways behind them, improving methods of diagnosis, and developing more effective treatments. Through cutting-edge research and patient-centered care, the Center works to bring new hope to individuals and families affected by rare diseases. Their vision is to create a future where lysosomal disorders are no longer a barrier to living a full and healthy life. By supporting patients both across the United States and internationally, the Center strives to improve quality of life, advance medical breakthroughs, and ensure that every patient has access to the care and support they deserve. Peter,

Senator Markwayne Mullin has been confirmed as Secretary of Homeland
Security, replacing Kristi Noem, doubling down on the same extreme
approach that has already caused harm and devastation in communities
across the country.

We saw this play out under Trump and Noem, including in Minnesota, where
fear tactics didn’t make communities safer — they devastated them.
Families were separated, communities felt less safe, and innocent
civilians were killed with no accountability from DHS officers.

Instead of fixing a broken system, Trump and his extremist administration
are still working to expand mass deportation efforts and refusing to hold
federal agents accountable. That’s what’s at stake here.

Mullin’s record shows that his reign will be no different. He has
supported efforts to end birthright citizenship, expand indefinite
detention without due process, and weaken long-standing constitutional
safeguards. He wants to normalize racial profiling, shield federal
enforcement from accountability, and use the machinery of government to
target vulnerable communities instead of protecting them.

At the Squad Victory Fund, we’re not staying silent. We’re organizing,
mobilizing, and backing progressive champions who are fighting back and
holding this administration accountable for their unchecked recklessness.

We know real safety comes from trust, transparency, and dignity, not from
policies that tear communities apart. That’s why our movement is rooted in
collective action — building something stronger than any one voice alone.
But we can’t take on this fight alone.
